model.name: Rust Software Factory
model.documentation: Architecture of the software factory itself: how a business need becomes rolled-out Rust software, with AI agents doing the work and a human holding the gates. Also holds the sample reservation domain the factory builds (epic #17 onward).

property.value: docs/architecture/model.xml (ADR 0009), built by scripts/archimate/build.sh; do not edit the .archimate by hand

element.name: Use cases (crate application)
element.documentation: One use case per user action, plus the ScheduleRepository port, whose single update operation changes the schedule atomically (ADR 0008).

element.name: Conductor agent (Fable)
element.documentation: Main Claude Code session, model claude-fable-5-2.

element.name: Persistence adapter (crate adapters-db)
element.documentation: Implements the ScheduleRepository port; in-memory for now, holding one lock for each whole update.

element.name: Domain (crate domain)
element.documentation: Pure business rules: time slots, no overlapping reservations, booking and cancelling in a Schedule.

element.name: GitHub
element.documentation: Issues, Project board, pull requests and Actions CI.

element.name: Hard worker (Opus)
element.documentation: Subagent on claude-opus-5-5 for ambiguous or cross-crate tasks.

element.name: HTTP adapter (crate adapters-http)
element.documentation: Maps HTTP requests to use cases and errors to status codes; no business rules.

element.name: Reservation service
element.documentation: The deployed application (crate app): wires the adapters into the use cases and serves HTTP.

element.name: Scout (Haiku)
element.documentation: Subagent on claude-haiku-5-5 for search and context gathering.

element.name: Simple worker (Sonnet)
element.documentation: Subagent on claude-sonnet-5-5 for clear, single-crate tasks.

element.name: Issue
element.documentation: Epic, story, requirement, task, bug, change request or ADR request.

element.name: Pull request
element.documentation: A proposed change with traceability links and test evidence.

element.name: Schedule
element.documentation: The day's reservations (domain type Schedule), changed only through the atomic update of ScheduleRepository (ADR 0008): read, change and store happen as one step, and a refused change stores nothing. Reservation ids are unique only within one running instance (storage is in memory).

element.name: Reservations HTTP API
element.documentation: JSON over HTTP: POST /reservations books a slot, DELETE /reservations/{id} cancels one, GET /health answers probes. Rule, not-found and storage errors carry an {error} JSON body; requests the framework rejects (a non-numeric id, malformed JSON) get a plain-text body (ADR 0007).

element.name: Book a slot
element.documentation: Use case BookSlot, POST /reservations: 201 with the new id; 409 on overlap; 422 on an invalid slot.

element.name: Cancel a reservation
element.documentation: DELETE /reservations/{id}: 204 No Content when removed; 404 Not Found with {error} when the id is unknown or already cancelled (ADR 0007).

element.name: Customer
element.documentation: Reserves and cancels time slots through the reservation API.

element.name: Human approver
element.documentation: Signs off architecture, merges PRs, promotes pilot to production.

element.name: Architecture decision record
element.documentation: Why a significant decision was made, and what else was considered.

element.name: Reservation
element.documentation: A time slot held by a customer, identified by its reservation id.

element.name: User story
element.documentation: A small piece of user-visible behaviour with Gherkin acceptance criteria.

element.name: Accept build
element.documentation: Acceptance tests run against the release image.

element.name: Cancel a reservation
element.documentation: Give up a reservation by its id so the slot is free for someone else. No refund, notification or deadline (out of scope of epic #17).

element.name: Pilot and roll out
element.documentation: Deploy to the pilot host, then to production after approval.

element.name: Implement task
element.documentation: Code and tests for one task on its own branch.

element.name: Software delivery lifecycle
element.documentation: From business need to production rollout.

element.name: Plan and design
element.documentation: Vision, epics, stories, architecture model and ADRs (TOGAF A–D).

element.name: Reserve a slot
element.documentation: Ask for a time slot; get a reservation id, or a refusal if the slot overlaps an existing reservation.

element.name: Review and merge
element.documentation: Automated gates plus human merge of the PR.

element.name: Conductor
element.documentation: Plans, designs the architecture, splits work into tasks and routes each to a worker.

element.name: Worker
element.documentation: Carries out one task in its own git worktree and delivers it as a PR.

element.name: Unused slots stay blocked
element.documentation: Customers who can no longer come have no way to free their slot, so nobody else can book it (epic #17).

element.name: Business needs change often
element.documentation: Business rules and priorities change; software must follow quickly without decaying.

element.name: Development cost under control
element.documentation: Expensive AI models are used only where their reasoning is needed.

element.name: Customers can free slots they no longer need
element.documentation: The schedule reflects who is really coming, so free time can be booked by others.

element.name: Healthy, maintainable software
element.documentation: Code stays easy to change over years: clear boundaries, strong tests, recorded decisions.

element.name: Every change is traceable
element.documentation: Any line of code can be traced back to the business need that caused it, and forward to its release.

element.name: Cancelled slot rebookable at once
element.documentation: Success measure of epic #17: a cancelled slot can be booked again immediately.

element.name: Every change through a reviewed PR
element.documentation: main is protected; nothing reaches it without a pull request and a human merge.

element.name: Cancel a reservation by its id
element.documentation: Only that reservation is removed and its slot is free at once; no history is kept (story #18).

element.name: Refuse cancelling an unknown reservation
element.documentation: Cancelling a reservation that does not exist, including cancelling the same one a second time, is refused and changes nothing (story #19).

element.name: Route tasks to models by difficulty
element.documentation: Simple, clear tasks go to Sonnet, hard ones to Opus, search to Haiku; the conductor runs on Fable.

element.name: Architecture documented in TOGAF / ArchiMate
element.documentation: Business, information and technology architecture is kept as an ArchiMate model and TOGAF documents, so business-side changes can be analysed.

element.name: Customer
element.documentation: A person who reserves time slots and wants to free a slot they can no longer use.

element.name: Front-desk manager
element.documentation: Decision maker for epic #17.

element.name: Product owner
element.documentation: The human who owns the business outcome and approves the factory's gates.

element.name: Pilot host
element.documentation: First deploy target for a release.

element.name: Production hosts
element.documentation: Receive the release after the pilot is approved.

element.name: Developer workstation
element.documentation: Arch Linux desktop or Ubuntu on WSL, set up by bootstrap.sh.

element.name: Container registry (GHCR)
element.documentation: Stores the release images, built once and promoted unchanged.

element.name: Archi
element.documentation: Builds the ArchiMate model and HTML report from the text model.

element.name: Podman
element.documentation: Runs the application containers on every host.

element.name: Rust toolchain
element.documentation: Pinned in rust-toolchain.toml, with cargo tools pinned in mise.toml.

relationship.documentation: The conductor agent performs the work of the Conductor role.
The hard worker agent performs the work of the Worker role.
The simple worker agent performs the work of the Worker role.

view.name: Factory overview
view.documentation: Business, application and technology layers of the factory, top to bottom.

view.name: Delivery lifecycle
view.documentation: Who does what in the delivery lifecycle.

view.name: Why the factory exists
view.documentation: Stakeholder, drivers, goals, principles and requirements behind the factory.

view.name: Reservations: cancel a reservation
view.documentation: Sample reservation domain, epic #17: why customers cancel, the business processes, and the crates and API that serve them. Technology is unchanged (see id-view-layered).
